draft.title: Primary and secondary data
card: Data collected first-hand by the person doing the investigation, such as running your own survey of students in your year level.
Data that someone else collected and that you then use, such as figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) or a published government report.
Secondary data must be judged before it is used. You did not control how it was collected, so you check who collected it, when, and whether it suits your statistical question.
The same kind of data can be either. The number of students who walk to school in your survey is primary. The same kind of figure read from an ABS table is secondary.
draft.remember: Primary data is what you collect yourself. Secondary data is what you take from others, so you must check it fits your question.

a.q: A student asks, "How do students in my year level get to school?" Which choice is primary data?
opts: Her own survey of students in her year level
Travel figures from an ABS report
A classmate's survey results she copies
A council report on how people travel to school
a.why: The student collects the answers first-hand by running her own survey, so this is primary data. The other three use data that other people collected, which makes them secondary data, even if the sources are reliable.

b.q: Priya surveys her Year 8 class in Alice Springs about how long they spend on homework. She then compares her results with an ABS report on student study time. Which statement is correct?
opts: Her survey is primary and the report is secondary
Her survey is secondary and the report is primary
Both are primary because both are about study time
Both are secondary because both are about students
b.why: Priya collected her own survey answers, so they are primary data for her. The ABS report was collected by others, and she must check it suits her question, so it is secondary. The topic of the data does not decide which kind it is.
b.clue: Ask who collected each set of data, not what it is about.

a.best: Her own survey of students in her year level

b.best: Her survey is primary and the report is secondary
